lesson_title: Assembling with Instructions: Diagrams, Parts Lists and the Plug Wired Wrong
hook_text: The iron heats up. The plug is wired WRONG. And nothing in the house will tell you — here's the check that will.
clip_script: Flat-pack cupboard, two boxes, not one sentence — just pictures giving commands. The exploded view hangs every part where it belongs; thin lines run from bolt to hole. Before you build: roll call. Twelve cam locks on the list, nine in the box? Three missing — two shelves lock, the third waits, and you found out BEFORE step 10 swallowed your afternoon. Now the order. Nail the back panel on early and the shelves have no face left to slide in through. That thin back sheet is also what keeps the corners square — skip it and your cupboard leans like it's exhausted. Steps that seal go LAST. Then the plug, where order becomes safety. Brown to live, right. Blue to neutral, left. Green-and-yellow to earth, the tall pin on top. Swap brown and blue and here's the horror: the iron still heats. Everything looks fine. But the switch is on the wrong wire now — the element stays LIVE with the switch off, waiting. Working is not the same as right. Check the colours, not the iron. And the money? Self-assembly saves R450 — if you have the four hands step 8 demands. A split door costs R520. Do that maths before the Allen key comes out.
visual_style: An exploded cupboard hanging in mid-air over a lounge floor, parts clicking home along thin guide lines; a parts list ticking itself; then an open plug in close-up, the brown and blue cores swapping with a red warning glow while the iron steams innocently.
mood: Hands-on and quietly serious — DIY swagger that turns protective at the plug.
pacing: Playful through the roll call and the leaning cupboard, then slowing hard at the plug for the safety reveal, closing quick on the R450-versus-R520 decision.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build anything the box throws at you — safely and in order.
